stories.headline: S&P 500, DOW HIT FRESH RECORDS AS ALPHABET'S $80B AI RAISE AND HPE'S 26% SURGE IGNITE RALLY
stories.body: U.S. equities extended their record run Tuesday, with the S&P 500 rising to 7,620 (+0.26%) and Nasdaq to 27,160 (+0.27%), as Alphabet announced an $80 billion equity raise — including an investment from Berkshire Hathaway — to fund AI infrastructure expansion, and HPE surged 26% after pulling its long-term financial targets forward by two years. Chipmakers gained 5% on AI infrastructure optimism; the 10-year yield ticked up 2 bps to 4.46%, but the growth narrative overwhelmed rate concerns.

stories.headline: IRAN TALKS REMAIN SUSPENDED; OIL HOLDS ABOVE $90 AS HORMUZ RISK PREMIUM PERSISTS
stories.body: WTI crude eased -1.1% to $91 Tuesday on a technical pullback, but Iran's halt of ceasefire negotiations with the U.S. has kept oil elevated two consecutive sessions. The IEA has characterized the Strait of Hormuz supply disruption as the largest in market history; traders are watching $93 as the level at which another leg up would meaningfully reprice 2026 PCE inflation forecasts and further delay Fed rate cuts.

stories.headline: NBA FINALS MEDIA DAY: WEMBY'S SPURS AWAIT BRUNSON'S KNICKS — GAME 1 WEDNESDAY 8:30 ET
stories.body: The 2026 NBA Finals Media Day unfolded in San Antonio on Tuesday, setting the stage for Game 1 Wednesday at 8:30 PM ET on ABC. The Knicks — in their first Finals since 1999 after sweeping Cleveland in the East — face Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs, who survived a seven-game Western Conference war with Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's Thunder to reach the franchise's sixth Finals appearance.

stories.headline: SEAHAWKS LOCK UP DERICK HALL ON 3YR/$42M EXTENSION AFTER SUPER BOWL LX HEROICS
stories.body: Seattle signed edge rusher Derick Hall to a three-year, $42 million contract with $21 million guaranteed, securing the 25-year-old who recorded two sacks and a forced fumble in the Seahawks' 29-13 Super Bowl LX win over New England. The deal is the lead NFL story on the league's June 2 news roundup; Seattle's OTAs continue through June 4 ahead of mandatory minicamp June 9-11.

stories.headline: PORTAL OFFSEASON TAKES STOCK: TEXAS, LSU LEAD CLASS RANKINGS; RUSSELL COMMITS TO UW
stories.body: A quiet June Tuesday in college football: Texas and LSU topped 2026 winter portal class rankings, each landing elite additions at QB and skill positions. Washington secured a commitment from Colorado OL Reis Russell this week. Huskies season opener vs. WSU is officially set for NBC on Sept. 6 at 1 PM PT; Big Ten single-game home tickets go on sale June 15.

stories.headline: MOMCILOVIC SPURNS NBA DRAFT, PICKS KENTUCKY; BLUE BLOODS DOMINATE SUMMER PORTAL
stories.body: Former Iowa State forward Milan Momcilovic withdrew from NBA Draft consideration and committed to Kentucky, ranked No. 3 in the transfer portal cycle. The Wildcats are assembling one of the portal's top classes this summer; Duke topped Andy Katz's initial Power 44 for 2026-27. Washington added SF Lattimore Ford (local commit), LeJuan Watts (Texas Tech), and a Gonzaga transfer as Sprinkle rebuilds for next season.

deepDive.title: The Jobs Report Is Friday — Here's Why NFP Moves the Entire Rate Path
content: Friday brings the May non-farm payrolls (NFP) report at 8:30 AM ET — one of the most market-moving data releases in any given month. With the 10-year Treasury yield at 4.46% and investors uncertain whether the Fed will cut rates at the June 17-18 FOMC meeting, the consensus estimate of approximately +150,000 new jobs sits at exactly the kind of threshold that can reprice the bond curve in real time. This context matters: it's not just a labor market data point, it's the primary input into the Fed's policy calculus three weeks from now.

Non-farm payrolls measure the net change in paid, non-farm employment across roughly 80% of the U.S. private workforce, surveyed by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. Markets translate the headline number into fed funds rate expectations almost instantly via the CME FedWatch tool. The mechanism: strong job growth (+200K+) signals a tight labor market, reducing the urgency for cuts, which raises short-end yields — the 2-year is most responsive — and typically lifts the dollar while pressuring equities. A weak print (<100K) does the opposite. Each 25 bps of expected Fed easing shifts the 2-year yield by roughly 15-20 bps, and rate-sensitive equity sectors like tech and real estate reprice accordingly.

What most investors underweight is that three sub-components often matter more than the headline: average hourly earnings (AHE), the unemployment rate, and labor force participation. During the 2022-2023 hiking cycle, the Fed raised 525 bps in 16 months partly because markets kept anchoring on headline job gains while AHE was printing +0.5% monthly, embedding wage-push inflation into services. Today, with WTI at $91 from the Iran conflict already adding supply-side inflationary pressure, a hot AHE print of +0.4% or above on Friday would effectively close the door on any 2026 rate cuts. The August 2024 NFP miss (+114K vs. 175K expected) moved the 2-year yield 30 bps in a single session — the largest single-day shift since 2008.

For Friday specifically, watch the sequence: (1) headline vs. +150K consensus, (2) AHE month-over-month vs. +0.3% expected, (3) unemployment vs. 4.2% expected. If all three come in soft, September becomes a live FOMC meeting for a cut and the 2-year yield could break below 3.9%. A combination of hot prints keeps June and July on hold, pushes the 10-year toward 4.6%, and adds further pressure to equities already pulling back from record levels. The bond market opens 10 minutes early at 8:20 AM ET; watching the 2-year in that pre-release window often reveals where institutional players are positioned ahead of the print.
